same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in

Thus, there must exist a prime number \( p \) that is greater than \( n \). Since \( n \) was chosen arbitrarily, this holds for all natural numbers \( n \), proving that there are infinitely many prime numbers.
